sentences.text: Shri Nitin Gupta - Government Advocate for the responde Heard on I.A.No.9747 of 2025, which is first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail under Section 430 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 on behalf of appellant.

This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of judgment dated 25/06/2022 passed by the Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Raisen (MP) in Special Case No.136/2020, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under :-
Conviction u/s Imprisonment Fine amount RI in default 366 of IPC RI for 5 years Rs.
5,000/- RI for 6 months 376(A)(B) of IPC RI for 20 years Rs.5,000/- RI for 6 months 5(m)/6 of POCSO Act RI for 20 years Rs.5000/- RI for 6 months 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act RI for 20 years Rs.5,000/- RI for 6 months
Learned counsel for the appellant is pointed out that father of the victim (PW-2) has admitted that his eldest son is 20 years of age.
Victim (PW-1) submits that her marriage was performed about one year back when she gave deposition on 06/01/2022.
Mother of the victim (PW-6) has admitted that there is age gap of 2 to 3 years amongst all her children.
Thus, when father of the victim states that his eldest son is 20 years of age and there is age gap of 2 to 3 years, then victim will be deemed to be adult at the 2 CRA-6229-2023 time of incident.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail.
Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Government Advocate opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the fact that there appears to be good chances of success in appeal, without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case to suspend the remaining part of jail sentence of appellant Azad Sahariya and Azad Sahariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171762983/
1 release him on bail.

sentences.text:
It is directed that on depositing fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on 02/12/2025 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the concerned Court, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL) (AVANINDRA  JUDGE J  mc Azad Sahariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171762983/
